name: A Simple and Effective Pruning Approach for Large Language Models
authors: Sun, Wang, Liu, Miller, Papailiopoulos, Wallis
problem: Magnitude pruning underperforms on LLMs, while second-order pruning methods need weight reconstruction that is expensive at billion-parameter scale.
mechanism: Wanda (Pruning by Weights and Activations): score each weight by |W_ij| * ||X_j||_2, where X_j is the INPUT ACTIVATION norm of channel j, and drop the lowest-scoring weights per output row. The score is computed directly from the pretrained weights and a single small calibration set of activations - NO retraining, NO weight update, NO gradient. The pruned model is used as-is. The metric is also invertible, so Wanda can be applied without access to the original weights (privacy-preserving transfer).
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract): evaluated on LLaMA and LLaMA-2 across various language benchmarks, Wanda 'significantly outperforms the established baseline of magnitude pruning' and 'performs competitively against recent method involving intensive weight update' - i.e. it matches SparseGPT-class methods while being training-free and gradient-free. COMPRESSION RATIO: unstructured sparsity at the level swept in the paper (up to ~50% typical for LLaMA-7B). QUALITY COST: reported as beating magnitude pruning with no quantitative delta in the abstract. Note again: UNSTRUCTURED sparsity yields memory savings but no acceleration on any current accelerator.
